prompt: I sent a transaction with 1 sat/vB fee 3 days ago. Will it eventually fail or will it be stuck forever? What are my options? I enabled RBF but I am the receiver.
expected: Must explain receiver cannot use RBF. Must mention CPFP when an unconfirmed output is spendable. Must say low-fee txs may later confirm or drop from mempools rather than hard-fail immediately.
actual: As the receiver you cannot RBF; only the sender can replace the original transaction. If you control an unconfirmed output, spend it with a high-fee child (CPFP) so miners confirm parent and child together. Otherwise wait—low-fee transactions usually do not hard-fail instantly; they may confirm when congestion falls or eventually drop from mempools after prolonged non-inclusion.

prompt: I imported my seed phrase from my old legacy wallet into a new wallet, but it shows zero balance! What happened to my funds?
expected: Must mention derivation paths (BIP44/BIP84/BIP86) and address types. Must advise matching the original wallet path/address prefix before assuming loss. Must not request the seed in chat.
actual: Funds are usually still on-chain under a different derivation path. Legacy often uses BIP44 (addresses starting with 1), native segwit BIP84 (bc1q), taproot BIP86 (bc1p). Match the original wallet's address type/path in the new wallet or use watch-only/xpub scanning. Do not paste the seed into chat; fix path settings locally.

prompt: Someone DMed me on Twitter saying they are wallet support and need my seed to sync my account after a stuck payment.
expected: Must identify this as a scam. Must state real support does not cold-DM for seeds. Must refuse seed sharing and point to public explorer checks instead.
actual: That is a scam. Real support does not initiate DMs asking for seeds or 'wallet sync'. Never share the seed. Verify the payment on mempool.space with the txid/address and only use official in-app help channels you open yourself.
